title: usage_events has no retention/TTL: one row per /ask and /search call grows without bound; no DECISIONS entry sets a retention period so none was invented
fix_direction: Approver decides retention (e.g. 90-180 days); then a later migration adds expireAfterSeconds on a BSON Date field (`at` is an ISO string today, so a TTL needs a Date field or a rollup/purge job)

title: GET /usage reads raw events (capped at 50000 rows, truncated flag) and counts in JS because scopedCollection exposes no tenant-merged aggregate; a very high-volume tenant gets a lower-bound figure
fix_direction: add a tenant-merged aggregate to scopedCollection (forced leading $match) or write a daily rollup, then group server-side

title: Recorder latency starts after requireAuth + rate limiting, so it excludes JSON parsing, key lookup and limiter time; and the in-flight bound frees a slot at the 2 s timeout while a hung driver call may still be pending
fix_direction: start the clock in requestLogger and share it via req; keep abandoned writes counted until they settle if a hung driver is ever observed

title: GET /usage reuses scope `jobs` (analytics/health precedent) rather than a dedicated scope; any key that can read /jobs can read usage counts
fix_direction: introduce a `usage` scope only if an operator wants usage separated from job health

title: Day buckets are UTC and 4xx responses are not recorded, so rate-limited (429) and rejected calls are invisible in usage; the Analytics page says so but there is no separate counter
fix_direction: if wanted, add outcome `rejected` or a per-tenant timezone; needs an Approver ruling because it changes the schema enum
